label: Sampling: integrating from noise to data
context: Left half and right half panels side by side (stack vertically on narrow widths), both showing a 1D-in-time picture: horizontal axis is t from 1 (noise, left) to 0 (data, right), vertical axis is x. The data distribution at t = 0 is two narrow modes at x = -1 and x = +1; at t = 1 a wide Gaussian. Left panel title 'curved paths (diffusion ODE)': about 14 trajectories from noise samples curve and fan out late toward the two modes. Right panel 'straight paths (rectified flow)': the same start points travel on nearly straight lines to the modes. Animate a dot along each trajectory. Then overlay Euler steps with 4 large steps on each: on the left the 4-step dots overshoot/miss the modes (draw them deviating), on the right they land on the modes. Caption: 'straighter paths need fewer steps'. Canvas is responsive: width anywhere from 340 to 900 px, height 400 px; derive every size and position from width and height, keep all text at least 11 px and fully inside the canvas, and on narrow widths stack or shrink rather than overlap. Loop forever on a cycle of 10 to 16 s with smooth easing between phases. White background. Put a one-line phase caption at the top centre that changes with the phase. No title inside the canvas (the card has one). Use plain sans-serif labels.

spec.title: Sampling: integrating from noise to data
spec.caption: Left: curved diffusion-ODE paths. Right: near-straight rectified-flow paths from the same noise samples. Four large Euler steps miss the modes on the curved paths and land on them on the straight ones, so straighter paths need fewer steps.
